notes.text: Petrochemical site beside a river estuary making base chemicals (ethylene, propylene) in a lower-olefins cracker, plus two styrene monomer / propylene oxide (SM/PO) plants. More than 800 employees.

SM/PO chemistry: ethylbenzene + oxygen gives ethylbenzene hydroperoxide; with propylene and a catalyst this gives propylene oxide, methylphenylcarbinol (MPC) and methylphenyl ketone (MPK). MPC is converted to styrene monomer. By-product MPK is converted back to MPC in a separate hydrogenation unit.

Plant N2 (the newer SM/PO plant, about 15 years in service; jointly owned, the site operator holds the permit) contains hydrogenation unit U-H, the subject of this package. Three sister plants abroad use virtually the same process.
U-H converts MPK to MPC with hydrogen over a catalyst. The reaction is exothermic; heat is removed by liquid ethylbenzene flowing over the catalyst.

Laboratory test (about 37 years ago, liquid-full reactor) found no reaction between ethylbenzene and catalyst; ethylbenzene is treated as inert in the unit's safety studies. Wetting/runaway risk was identified for the reduction and production phases; no pressure relief is sized for a runaway.
Safety report scenarios for plant N2 (10 scenarios) include none for U-H. Reactive hazard assessment (3–4 years ago) focused on the styrene monomer section.

Sister-plant history (4 years ago, same unit type, Catalyst B): temperature excursion during the heating phase to more than 685 °C with the flare discharge closed; attributed by the company to a leaking hydrogen valve.

chemicals.name: Catalyst B (Cu/Cr/Ba pellets: copper oxide and barium chromate)

notes.text: Catalyst (both reactors): cylindrical pellets containing copper, chromium and barium (copper oxide and barium chromate). Replaced every few years as activity declines. Current product "Catalyst B" from a supplier selected about 14 years ago as a drop-in replacement for the original "Catalyst A" (no equipment or procedure changes). Catalyst A hexavalent chromium content 0.1–0.2 wt%. Catalyst B: about 3 years ago the manufacturer changed its manufacturing process; hexavalent chromium content up to 5 wt% (within the agreed specification; shown in the safety data sheet). Catalyst selection tests (about 15 years ago) were dry reductions with H2/N2 without ethylbenzene, focused on normal production.
Catalyst pellets (Cu/Cr/Ba), fresh charge in both reactors.
Catalyst A hexavalent chromium content 0.1–0.2 wt%.

The work instructions do not state a heating rate or a nitrogen flow. The control system is configured for normal production; there are no automated control loops for heating; start-up is under manual control. Separator level control is in manual mode during start-up.
Operating philosophy: Stabilise, Slow down, Stop when limits are exceeded; during start-up the duty to intervene may be waived only if this does not create an unsafe situation.
Heating rate for start-up heating phase: 30 °C/h.

steps.text: Flush with ethylbenzene to remove contamination.
Fill with clean ethylbenzene and circulate (circulation phase).
Reduce the catalyst with hydrogen; only at the correct temperature and after at least 6 h of hot ethylbenzene circulation.

notes.text: Plant N2 has been shut down for a short "pit stop" (started 9 days ago); main task: replacing the catalyst pellets in R-1 and R-2.
This evening: start-up of U-H per the job analysis — fill V-1 and V-2 with ethylbenzene, start circulation, then heat.
The panel operator, production team leader and process engineer have agreed a heating rate of 50 °C/h, adjusted manually.
Nitrogen to the distribution plates set at about 240 kg/h.

This is the first catalyst-change start-up for both the panel operator and the production team leader (U-H is started after a catalyst change once every 3–4 years). Earlier stops showed flows and levels are unstable in manual mode during start-up.
Neither the catalyst change nor the start-up parameters have been put through the management-of-change procedure.
